endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Evaluate whether AI model threshold selection has been justified and note whether a risk assessment plan has been developed, documented and conducted.

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Documentation should include the results of testing against predefined metrics, identified data gaps, and the effectiveness of implemented risk mitigation controls.

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Provide risk management file | Including identified risks, mitigation measures, monitoring measures

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
endorsements.quote: Therefore, FDA also recommends that sponsors 688 incorporate the considerations outlined in the FDA-recognized voluntary consensus standard of 689 AAMI CR34971 Guidance on the Application of ISO 14971 to Artificial Intelligence and 690 Machine Learning, which is specific to AI-enabled devices.

commentary.bottom_line: Four frameworks and guidance documents, including an FDA draft guidance, recommend documented AI risk assessment plans and results, but no supplied study tests whether the practice reduces harm or improves risk tracking. No supplied study documents the hazard of ad hoc, untracked risk activities either, so the recommendation rests on consensus and regulatory expectation alone.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The four endorsements agree in direction, and that agreement reflects expert consensus rather than measured effects on patient outcomes, error detection, or the completeness of risk records.

The FDA draft guidance on AI-enabled device software functions recommends that sponsors apply AAMI CR34971, the recognized standard adapting ISO 14971 risk management to machine learning. For device sponsors, a documented risk file may therefore become a submission expectation. FUTURE-AI and the CHAI guides extend similar documentation expectations to deployers outside FDA jurisdiction, though these carry no legal force.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares organizations or AI deployments with and without documented, lifecycle-updated risk assessment plans. Useful designs would measure whether such documentation changes how often deployment risks, data gaps, or failed controls are detected before patient harm, and what staff time the documentation requires.
commentary.underserved_note: No supplied study tested the practice in any population, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy settings. Health systems serving these groups cannot tell from this evidence whether documented risk plans identify data gaps affecting their patients, and they may need to require that risk files address subgroup performance explicitly.
